mainTopic: The end of the משנה on the burned bulls and goats, and why the משנה leaves out collecting the blood in a כלי שרת in the north: the אשם מצורע, whose blood is collected both by hand and in a vessel.
overview: The amud opens with the end of the משנה about the פרים הנשרפים and שעירים הנשרפים. Every blood placement is essential. The leftover blood is poured on the western יסוד of the outer altar, but skipping that does not disqualify. All these animals are then burned at the בית הדשן. The גמרא asks why the משנה's opening rule for קדשי קדשים mentions only שחיטה in the north and not collecting the blood in a כלי שרת in the north. It answers that the תנא left this out because the אשם מצורע has its blood collected by hand. A later משנה does require a vessel for the אשם מצורע, so the גמרא explains that this offering has both kinds of collection. A ברייתא proves it: the blood placed on the מצורע's ear, thumb and toe is taken by hand, and the blood for the מזבח is taken in a vessel, because the אשם is compared to a חטאת. So two כהנים collect its blood, one by hand and one in a כלי.

steps.title: Every placement is required; the leftover blood is not
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes the blood service of the burned bulls and goats. Each placement is essential, but pouring the leftover blood is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even one of their blood placements, if missing, disqualifies the offering. The leftover blood the כהן would pour on the western base of the outer altar, and if he did not pour it, that does not disqualify.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is closing its description of the blood service for the פרים הנשרפים and שעירים הנשרפים. It tells us which parts are essential and which are not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels here. The blood placements themselves are מעכב, so missing even one ruins the offering. The שיריים, the leftover blood poured on the יסוד, is a מצוה but not מעכב.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each placement is essential. Pouring the leftover blood on the western יסוד is not essential.

steps.title: All of them are burned at the place of the ashes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by saying that both groups of animals are burned at the בית הדשן.
steps.simpleTranslation: These and those are burned at the place of the ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes by telling us where these animals end up: they are burned at the בית הדשן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "These and those" groups the bull and goat of יום כיפור together with the other burned bulls and goats. They are not eaten. They are burned outside at the place where the altar ashes are taken.

steps.whatToRemember: The burned bulls and goats need every blood placement, and then they are burned at the בית הדשן.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both the יום כיפור bull and goat and the other burned bulls and goats are burned at the בית הדשן.

steps.title: Why not also mention collecting the blood in a vessel in the north?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה's opening rule for קדשי קדשים does not also say their blood is collected in a כלי שרת in the north.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא: Let the משנה also teach that collecting their blood is done in a service vessel in the north!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It goes back to the start of the משנה, which said קדשי קדשים are slaughtered in the north, and asks why קבלה in a vessel in the north was not listed too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Collecting the blood is a required step of the service, just like slaughtering. So the reader expects the משנה to state the rule for קבלה as well. Its silence needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: And let it also teach: the גמרא asks why something was left out
Collecting their blood (קבלה)
A service vessel used in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.english: and the collection of their blood is in a service vessel in the north!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה's opening principle.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה's general rule for קדשי קדשים leaves out קבלה in a כלי שרת in the north.

steps.title: Left out because of the guilt offering of a מצורע
steps.stepSummary: The תנא left it out because the אשם מצורע has its blood collected by hand, so the rule would not hold for every case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since there is the אשם מצורע, whose blood is collected by hand, he left it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's rule is meant to cover all קדשי קדשים. The אשם מצורע does not fit a rule saying the blood is collected in a vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A general rule cannot be stated if one member of the group is an exception. The אשם מצורע is still one of the קדשי קדשים, but in its case the blood is caught in the כהן's hand. So the תנא chose not to state the vessel rule.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the אשם מצורע's blood is collected by hand, a universal vessel rule could not be stated.

steps.title: But a later משנה requires a vessel for the מצורע's offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this from a later משנה that says the אשם מצורע's blood is collected in a כלי שרת in the north.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is it not so? But it teaches later: the guilt offering of a נזיר and the guilt offering of a מצורע are slaughtered in the north, and their blood is collected in a service vessel in the north!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. A later משנה clearly says the אשם מצורע's blood does go in a vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 4 assumed the אשם מצורע is collected only by hand. The later משנה shows the same תנא requires a כלי שרת for it. So why would the אשם מצורע stop him from stating the rule here?

keyTerms.meaning: And is it not so? A surprised challenge
But it teaches
Later on, further in the text

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the אשם מצורע's blood is collected by hand and not in a vessel.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A later משנה explicitly requires a כלי שרת in the north for the אשם מצורע, so it should not block the general rule.

steps.title: First left out, then taught
steps.stepSummary: The תנא first left it out because part of the blood is collected by hand. Since some blood can only be collected in a vessel, he later taught it.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first he held that its blood is collected by hand, so he left it out. But since it cannot be done without a vessel, he went back and taught it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. Both משניות are right, because the אשם מצורע has both kinds of collection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אשם מצורע has blood collected by hand, and also blood that can only be collected in a vessel. Here, thinking of the hand part, the תנא did not make a universal vessel rule. In the later משנה, he focused on the part that needs a vessel and stated it.

keyTerms.meaning: At first, originally
He held, he thought
It is not possible except with
He went back and taught it

steps.whatToRemember: The אשם מצורע is still one of the קדשי קדשים, but its blood collection is unusual: partly by hand, partly in a vessel. That explains why the משנה leaves out the vessel rule here but states it later.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the אשם מצורע needs no vessel at all. Part of its blood is caught by hand, and part must go in a כלי שרת.

phrases.english: But since it cannot be done except with a vessel,

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִיקָּרָא סָבַר קִיבּוּל דָּמוֹ בַּיָּד הוּא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two aspects of one case: each משנה focuses on a different part of the אשם מצורע's blood collection.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות contradict each other about whether the אשם מצורע needs a vessel.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because some of its blood is caught by hand, the תנא did not state a universal vessel rule here. Because some of its blood requires a vessel, he states the vessel rule later.

steps.title: The blood for the מצורע is taken by hand
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word ״וְנָתַן״ that the כהן takes the אשם מצורע's blood with his own hand, not with a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: The פסוק says 'and he shall take.' You might think he takes the blood in a vessel. So the פסוק says 'and he shall put.' Just as the putting is done with the כהן's own body, so too the taking is done with the כהן's own body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove what it said in Step 6, that part of the אשם מצורע's blood is collected by hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא compares two words in the same פסוק: 'take' and 'put.' The putting of blood on the מצורע's ear, thumb and toe is clearly done with the כהן's finger. So the taking must also be done with his hand, not with a כלי.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought

With the כהן's own body, meaning his hand

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is only talking about the blood that goes on the מצורע's body. It is not saying that all the blood of the אשם מצורע is taken by hand. The next line deals with the blood for the מזבח.

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'And he shall take.' One might think he takes it in a vessel?

steps.title: The blood for the מזבח needs a vessel
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that the blood for the מזבח still needs a כלי, because the אשם is compared to a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the blood for the מזבח is also taken by hand. So the פסוק says: 'For like the חטאת, so is the אשם.' Just as a חטאת needs a vessel, so too an אשם needs a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going. It asks whether the blood for the מזבח is also taken by hand, and answers no, it needs a vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'by hand' rule could have spread to all the blood. The פסוק compares the אשם to a חטאת, and a חטאת's blood is collected in a כלי. So the blood that goes on the מזבח is collected in a vessel, and this fits the later משנה from Step 5.

'For like the חטאת, so is the אשם' (ויקרא 14:13)
Requires a vessel

steps.title: Two כהנים collect the blood, one by hand and one with a vessel
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that two כהנים collect the אשם מצורע's blood. The one with the vessel goes to the מזבח, and the one with his hand goes to the מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it comes out: for the אשם מצורע, two כהנים collect its blood, one by hand and one in a vessel. The one who collected it in a vessel goes to the מזבח, and the one who collected it by hand goes to the מצורע.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא puts both rules together and describes how it is actually done: two כהנים, two ways of collecting the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 7 and 8 looked like they might clash: by hand, or in a vessel? Both are true, for different uses of the blood. This explains Step 6: the תנא first left out 'in a כלי' because of the hand-collected part, and later taught it because of the vessel part.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes out that you say (a summing-up phrase)

Collect (the blood)

steps.whatToRemember: The אשם מצורע's blood is collected twice. It is collected by hand for placing on the מצורע's ear, thumb and toe, and in a כלי for the מזבח. That is why the משנה both leaves out and later includes 'in a כלי שרת.'

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Two כהנים collect the אשם מצורע's blood, one by hand for the מצורע and one in a כלי for the מזבח. This fully supports the answer in Step 6.
